title: Server originals are never pruned and every referenced original is re-uploaded on each push; owner quota can be exhausted with no browser remedy
trigger: Over the life of one owner token, import and later delete records (or record a few audio memories and delete them), pushing after each change; or let several conflicting (409) pushes upload originals. Each push re-sends every original still referenced by the snapshot; originals of deleted records, and originals uploaded by a push whose CAS later failed, stay on the server forever.
smallest_fix: Before each upload, skip originals whose id the server already holds (a HEAD/GET-by-id probe or a server-returned attachment index), and after a successful push delete server attachments that the pushed snapshot no longer references (api.deleteAttachment is already implemented). Alternatively document the cap and provide an explicit 'remove unreferenced server originals' action.
regression_check: Store test: push twice with an unchanged snapshot and assert uploadAttachment is called once per original on the first push and zero times on the second; delete a record, push, and assert deleteAttachment is called for its filename. Server-side: after those pushes the owner document's attachment count equals the number of referenced originals.
dependency_and_coordination: Independent focused commit in assigned owner's worktree; rebase before review.
evidence: Source proof: store.ts:520-524 (upload loop), store.ts:23-36 (APITransport lacks delete operations), api.ts:224-226 and 249-252 (unused delete methods), server/Sources/RevaServer/LocalFileStore.swift:110-121 (quota counts orphans), server/Sources/RevaServer/Models.swift:126-128 (caps). Bounded measurement from the snapshot: seed references 9 distinct originals totalling 618,312 bytes (python over apps/ios/Reva/Resources/{seed,fixture-manifest}.json). Refutation attempt: checked whether uploads are idempotent no-ops server-side (they overwrite the same id, so bytes are not duplicated) and whether the seed alone could hit the cap (it cannot: 9 files); the finding therefore concerns long-lived owners and failed pushes, hence P2 candidate rather than confirmed main-path defect. | Independent validation: core/store.ts:520-524; server LocalFileStore.swift:108-121; browser README.md:56; RecordDetail.tsx:284-286 documents retained originals.
